figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic illustration of the PTFE ﬁbrillation-based DPE fabrication process with an aqueous primer layer coating step. The primer layer is ﬁrst coated on the current collector using a water-based slurry and fully dried before lamination with the solvent-free DPE. The primer layer enables robust interfacial adhesion and eﬃcient electron conduction from the current collector to the DPE.

Figure 2. Design and structural characterization of carbon-based primer layers for dry electrodes. (a) Schematic illustration of the primer layer archi- tecture for a robust interface and the experimental design used to investigate the eﬀect of the primer layer on the electrochemical performance of DPEs. Cross-sectional SEM images of dry electrodes (b) without a primer layer and (c–g) with primer layers composed of (c) S100, (d) S75C25, (e) S50C50, (f) S25C75, and (g) C100. (h) Photograph of the SAICAS setup for measuring interfacial adhesion force. (i) Interfacial adhesion strength at 300 μm cutting depth and (j) the corresponding summary plot.

Figure 3. Surface morphology and mechanical properties of carbon-based primer layers. (a) Top-view SEM images, (b) 2D AFM images, (c) 3D AFM topographic images, and (d) AFM line-scan proﬁles of primer layers comprising (1) S100, (2) S75C25, (3) S50C50, (4) S25C75, and (5) C100. The AFM scan area was 50 × 50 μm2. (e) Hardness, (f) elastic modulus, and (g) elastic recovery ratio derived from nanoindentation measurements.

Figure 4. Microstructure-informed modeling and electron transport behavior in carbon-based primer layers. (a) Schematic illustration of the AFM topology-based 3D structure generation process: (i) surface topology measurement using AFM, (ii) primer layer reconstruction based on the acquired AFM topological map, and (iii) electrode microstructure modeling based on digital twin technology. (b) Potential distribution and (c) normalized current density, deﬁned as the local current density divided by the average current density, along the electrode thickness direction for S100, S50C50, and C100 calculated from electron conduction simulations. (d) 3D current density distribution. (e) 3D distribution and (f) 1D distribution along the thickness direction of active materials exposed to the high current density (top 10% current density).

Figure 5. Electrochemical characterization and XPS analysis of dry electrodes. (a) Rate performance at C-rates ranging from 0.2 to 7.0C (charge rate: 0.5C). (b) Long-term cycling performance at 1C. (c) Nyquist plots of EIS measured after cycling. XPS results of (d) F 1s, (e) O 1s, and (f) C 1s spectra for each electrode after cycling. (g) Schematic illustration of the electron transport behavior without a primer layer and with S100, S50C50, and C100 primer layers, with the corresponding radar chart shown in (h).
